name: Charles Brown
description:
'''Tony Russell''' "'''Charles'''" '''Brown''' (September 13, 1922 – January 21, 1999) was an American singer and pianist whose soft-toned, slow-paced nightclub style influenced [[West Coast blues]] in the 1940s and 1950s. Between 1949 and 1952, Brown had seven Top 10 hits in the U.S. ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B]] [[record chart|chart]]. His best-selling recordings included "[[Driftin' Blues]]", "[[Merry Christmas Baby]]" and  "[[Please Come Home for Christmas]]".

For his contribution to the blues genre, Brown was inducted into the [[Blues Hall of Fame]] (1996) and into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] (1999). Through his career, Brown received three [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] nominations for [[Best Traditional Blues Album]] for the albums [[All My Life (Charles Brown album)|''All My Life'']] (1990), ''Someone To Love'' (1992) and ''Charles Brown's Cool Christmas Blues'' (1996)'','' and won three [[Blues Music Awards]].
